result.summary: The page is mostly well-structured, but there are a few visual problems: the promotional banner has severely low-contrast white text on a pale green background, a category filter chip is cut off at the screen edge with no visible label, and a restaurant name in the horizontal carousel is truncated without an ellipsis.

issues.description: The promo banner text '3 free deliveries for you' and 'Use code TALLINN3 at checkout · min. order €10' is white/very light on a pale mint-green background, making it nearly unreadable and failing contrast requirements.
issues.suggestion: Use a dark text color (e.g., dark green or near-black) on the light green banner, or darken the banner background so white text meets WCAG contrast ratios (4.5:1 for body text).

issues.description: A sixth category filter chip on the right edge (after 'Healthy') is clipped so only a sliver of the pill is visible with no readable label, which looks broken rather than like an intentional scroll affordance.
issues.suggestion: Adjust chip spacing/peek amount so a meaningful portion of the next chip (including part of its label) is visible, or add a fade/gradient edge to signal horizontal scrolling.

issues.description: In the 'Fastest near you' carousel, the third restaurant name appears as 'Trattoria Piccol', truncated at the screen edge without an ellipsis, making the text look cut off/broken.
issues.suggestion: Constrain the label to the card width and apply text truncation with an ellipsis (e.g., 'Trattoria Picco…'), or wrap the name to a second line.

issues.description: The bottom pizza restaurant card is partially hidden behind the bottom navigation bar with its content (name, rating) not visible, which can appear broken in a static view.
issues.suggestion: Add bottom padding equal to the nav bar height to the scroll container so the last card is not overlapped when scrolled to the end.
